# Vendored: OmniVoice `lang_map.py`

`lang_map.py` is a **byte-identical** copy of

    https://github.com/k2-fsa/OmniVoice/blob/main/omnivoice/utils/lang_map.py

| | |
|---|---|
| upstream commit | `c8c0a6257b9b652dc7d239df9d911dbb1f9dabdf` (2026-04-01) |
| git blob sha1 | `ffcda10ae5ab93ac45ca12de1147a752585a5ed1` |
| license | Apache-2.0 (header retained in the file; see `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt`) |

## Why it is here

`src/core/omnivoice_lang_table.h` is generated from this file, and the language
IDs in it are not cosmetic: OmniVoice carries the target language as a literal
string in its prompt, so a wrong or unresolved value conditions the model on
tokens it never saw in that slot (SubtitleEdit-13273).

Vendoring makes `tools/gen-omnivoice-lang-map.py --check` **hermetic**, so CI can
gate the generated header against its source without a network call. Fetching
upstream at check time would have made the gate flaky, and a gate CI cannot run
is a gate that ships wrong.

## Keep it byte-identical

Do not edit this file. The blob sha1 above is what
`--check-upstream` compares against the GitHub API, which is only an exact test
while the copy is unmodified. To take a new upstream revision:

```bash
python tools/gen-omnivoice-lang-map.py --update-vendored   # refetch + regenerate
```

then update the two hashes and the date in the table above, and re-read the
diff — new languages are additions we want, but a *changed* ID for an existing
language would silently alter what every caller of that name synthesises.
